clue.text: Naval officer in a frenzy — one has lost faith

indicators.note: in tells us the officer's letters sit inside the phrase for a frenzy

parts.note: to be in a state is to be in a frenzy
PO is a Petty Officer in the navy

explanation.surface: A naval officer worked up into a frenzy has lost his religious faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade who abandons a religion or cause is exactly one who has lost faith.

clue.text: Desire shown in obscure language used by politician

indicators.note: used by puts the language after the politician, as his possession following him

parts.note: LIB is short for a Liberal politician
Ido is a little-known artificial language derived from Esperanto

explanation.surface: Desire is betrayed by the obscure jargon a politician uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Freudian term for sexual drive or appetite, hence desire.

clue.text: Sudden pain that has mammals rolling over

indicators.note: rolling over turns the flying mammals' word end to end

parts.note: bats are flying mammals

explanation.surface: A sudden pain makes the mammals roll over.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab of pain is a sharp sudden twinge.

clue.text: Maybe wife grabs a kiss lying in bed?

indicators.note: grabs means the relative holds the following letters within

parts.note: a wife is one example of a relation by marriage
X is the conventional kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Perhaps a wife snatches a kiss while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in bed is an instance of rest and repose, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Competent manager, I am able to get hold of name of astronomer

indicators.note: to get hold of means the preceding letters clasp the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a coper is someone who manages or copes competently
can means am able

explanation.surface: A capable manager boasts he can grasp the name of an astronomer.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronomer is Copernicus; the answer is the adjective relating to him, so 'of astronomer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describing things belonging to the Polish stargazer Copernicus, such as his heliocentric system.

clue.text: Obsequious type, willing follower in want of leader

indicators.note: in want of leader means the first letter is lost from the follower's word

parts.note: a sheep follows the flock willingly

explanation.surface: A fawning character is a willing follower with no one to lead him.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the creepily humble clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Uriah Heep is the archetype of the fawning, ever-so-humble sycophant.

clue.text: Minimal power needed by men: bit of furniture easy to move?

parts.note: a small p is the abbreviation for power
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Little power is needed by the men, as this bit of furniture moves easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable means able to be carried around, so easy to move.

clue.text: Offensive husband accepts responsibility? The reverse

indicators.note: accepts would put the responsibility inside the husband's letter
The reverse swaps the roles, so the trust word takes in the single letter instead

parts.note: trust is a charge or responsibility placed on someone

explanation.surface: A husband takes on responsibility, or perhaps it is the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrust is an attack or push forward, the noun sense of an offensive.

clue.text: One half of an island? The woman gets nothing!

indicators.note: One half of keeps three of the six letters and drops the rest

parts.note: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: She is left with one half of an island and nothing more!
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a zero, a figure meaning nothing.

clue.text: Change during which one gets negative and sour

indicators.note: during which means the following letters occur in the middle of the change word

parts.note: to vary is to change
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A change in which someone becomes negative and sour-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegary means acid-tasting or, of temper, sharp and sour.

clue.text: After a while little woman shows spell

indicators.note: After places the little woman behind the short while

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a while
Jo is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: After a while the little woman shows a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Mojo is a magic charm or spell, especially in blues culture.

clue.text: Spring month: Bishop and king open that landmark in capital

indicators.note: open means the bishop and king split the month apart by entering it

parts.note: March is a spring month
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: In a spring month a bishop and king open a landmark in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: MARBLE ARCH is a monumental white arch in central London, at the corner of Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous triumphal arch near Hyde Park is a landmark in London, the capital.

clue.text: Officer at the side providing a form of security

parts.note: COL is short for colonel, an officer
lateral means at the side

explanation.surface: An officer stands at the side providing a kind of security.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security against a loan.

clue.text: Pouting expression of shy person, son being put out

indicators.note: being put out means the son's letter is ejected from the shy person

parts.note: a mouse is a timid, shy person

explanation.surface: A shy person pouts because her son is being thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: A moue is a little pout or grimace made with the lips.

clue.text: Leader of infamous county set's abandoned compound

indicators.note: Leader of picks the opening letter of infamous
abandoned means the set's letters have gone from the county

parts.note: Somerset is an English county in the south-west
set's is read as set has, the group of letters removed

explanation.surface: The leader of a notorious county set has abandoned the compound.
explanation.definitionFit: An isomer is a chemical compound sharing a formula with another but with a different structure.

clue.text: Accompanied little fellow, about twenty, keeping close to parent

indicators.note: about means the little fellow wraps around everything else

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward

indicators.note: keeping means the twenty holds the following letter inside

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: close to selects the final letter of parent

explanation.surface: A little chap of about twenty, staying close to a parent, was accompanied.
explanation.definitionFit: To be escorted is to be accompanied by someone, often for protection.

clue.text: Favourite boy keeps diary — hard things being studied?

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: keeps means the boy's name holds the diary inside it

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
a log is a diary or record

explanation.surface: A favourite boy keeps a diary of the hard things he studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrology is the study of rocks, which are hard things, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: E.g. French national?

definitions.meaning: French is an example of a school discipline
a national, such as a citizen of France, owes allegiance to a state

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests a French citizen; split, it is a school course and a citizen of a state.
explanation.definitionFit: A school discipline and a person owing allegiance to a monarch or state are both senses of the word.

clue.text: A lord — no leader, a leader's brother

indicators.note: no leader means the lord loses his first letter

parts.note: a baron is a lord

explanation.surface: A lord with no leader — yet a leader's brother.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Aaron was the brother of Moses, the leader of the Israelites.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical Aaron was the brother of Moses, who led the Israelites out of Egypt.

clue.text: Angler's equipment has missed river fish

indicators.note: has missed means the river's letter is left out of the equipment

parts.note: a reel is part of an angler's tackle

explanation.surface: The angler's gear has missed a river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a snakelike fish.

clue.text: Heather not upset about old lover — beginning of struggle for independence

indicators.note: about means the heather wraps around the old lover

parts.note: ling is a type of heather
an ex is a former lover

indicators.note: upset turns the word not upside down in a down entry

explanation.surface: Heather, not upset about an old lover, starts a struggle for independence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Lexington, Massachusetts, in 1775 was the first fight of the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: The skirmish at Lexington in 1775 opened the American Revolutionary War, the colonies' fight for independence.

clue.text: Cruel type, however beloved of Parisians

parts.note: but means however
cher is French for dear or beloved

explanation.surface: A cruel type, though dear to Parisians.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher is figuratively a brutal person who kills ruthlessly.

clue.text: Daughter needs to travel about in a crowd

parts.note: to rove is to wander or travel about

explanation.surface: A daughter has to roam around in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a large herd or moving crowd of people or animals.

clue.text: King Charles about to depart — here's the chopper

indicators.note: about means the king's abbreviation surrounds the departing word

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles
to leave is to depart

explanation.surface: King Charles is about to leave, and here is the axe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Charles I and the executioner's chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy chopping knife used by butchers.

clue.text: Instrument for the front porch? Order one finally in deal

indicators.note: in places the order and final letter inside the deal

parts.note: to barter is to deal or trade
OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of one

explanation.surface: An instrument for the front porch, with an Order finally included in the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: A weather front is what the instrument detects; the porch is a playful red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer measures air pressure, forecasting the arrival of a weather front, perhaps hung in a porch.

clue.text: Organise street — rift when about to replace parking

indicators.note: about gives the letter C, which takes the place of the P for parking

parts.note: a rupture is a rift or break

explanation.surface: Organise the street, with a rift when about to replace the parking.
explanation.definitionFit: To structure something is to arrange or organise it.

clue.text: Thug terribly loud invading domicile cut short

indicators.note: invading means the scrambled word enters the shortened home
cut short means the home loses its final letter

parts.note: home is a domicile

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of loud are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thug invades a house, making a terrible noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' reads as the thug's noise but is the fodder: 'terribly' rearranges it as ODLU, which 'invading' puts inside the docked HOM ('cut short').
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a gangster or violent street thug.

clue.text: Good memory, memory built up in school

parts.note: RAM is computer memory

indicators.note: built up in a down clue means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RAM again, computer memory

explanation.surface: Good memory, and memory built up at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammar school is the British selective secondary school, so the word can stand for school.

clue.text: Music-makers, nomads in the East End?

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: hoboes are wandering tramps or nomads

explanation.surface: Wandering musicians as nomads might be described in Cockney London.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney district of London, whose speech drops the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments, things that make music.

clue.text: Not entirely well, I lack colour

indicators.note: Not entirely says only part of the run of words is used

explanation.surface: Not entirely well, I look pale and lack colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple colour, named after the shrub.

clue.text: Crop you will get after end of summer

indicators.note: get after places the old word for you behind that letter
end of picks the final letter of summer

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: You will get the crop in after the end of summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal grain grown as a field crop.
